overview: A day dominated by widening Gulf hostilities, a sharp Miami air collision, a first-of-its-kind SpaceX catch, and a heated Indian political row over democracy, while markets are in a weekly winning run tempered by crude and the rupee.

items.headline: SpaceX's Starship is caught by launchpad arms in a first
items.summary: SpaceX's Starship returned from orbit and was caught by the mechanical arms of its launch tower, a first for the programme.
items.detail: Reports describe Starship coming back to the launch pad from orbit and being captured by the launchpad arms, a manoeuvre no vehicle of this kind had managed before. Earlier in the same flight the vehicle had reached orbit, though its booster was lost in the Gulf of Mexico. The catch was widely covered as a dramatic demonstration of the company's ambitions. Outlets have described the day as a victory for the company's test programme.
items.analysis: Catching a returning rocket rather than landing it on legs is meant to make reuse faster and cheaper, which matters for the economics of heavy launches. Watch for whether the booster problem is solved on the next flight.

items.headline: Iran attacks Bahrain as the regional conflict escalates
items.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guards claimed a drone attack on a US military site in Bahrain, which Bahrain says it intercepted, with sirens sounding across the island.
items.detail: Bahrain sounded alerts after Iran's Guards said they had targeted a US base, and Iran reportedly struck a US military site in the Gulf for the first time in two months. The move comes as hopes for a diplomatic deal are reported to be fading. Separately, Saudi-led forces said they had intercepted missiles and drones in the region. Bahrain hosts a major US naval presence, which is why attacks on it carry wider weight.
items.analysis: The strike is the first of its kind in two months, which raises the risk of further tit-for-tat attacks across Gulf states. Diplomatic signals in the coming days will be important.

items.headline: US seeks 24 years for Nikhil Gupta in Pannun murder plot case
items.summary: US prosecutors are seeking a 24-year jail term for Nikhil Gupta over an alleged plot to murder Sikh separatist Gurpatwant Singh Pannun, while the defence asks for 12 years.
items.detail: The sentencing request is in a US federal case in which Gupta is accused of plotting the killing of Pannun, a US-based activist. In a letter to the US judge, Gupta reportedly said he planned the operation alone. His lawyers have asked for a lighter sentence and asked the court to treat him humanely. The judge will decide the sentence after weighing both sides.
items.analysis: The case has been a point of friction in US-India security cooperation, and the sentence will be closely watched in both countries. The gap between the two sentencing requests is large.

items.headline: Two planes collide at Miami airport
items.summary: A UPS cargo plane and a passenger jet collided at Miami International Airport, with a passenger sharing footage of a crushed aircraft nose.
items.detail: Reports say the collision happened on a runway crossing, and one pilot's audio recorded after the impact was widely shared. The incident came a day after a nationwide US flight ground stop that was later blamed on a copper wire upgrade, according to the US transport secretary. Officials have not yet been quoted in these headlines on the cause of the Miami collision.
items.analysis: Coming so soon after the nationwide disruption, the crash raises questions about the safety of US airport operations, and investigators' findings will matter for airlines and insurers.

items.headline: Israeli strike kills senior Hamas commander in Gaza
items.summary: The Israeli military says it struck a senior Hamas commander in Gaza, whom Hamas has named as the Rafah Brigade chief.
items.detail: Israel described the commander as a senior armed figure and linked him to planning and overseeing the October 7 attack, according to reports. Hamas identified the man as Samir Abu Younis, the chief of its Rafah Brigade. The strike adds to a long-running pattern of targeted killings in the Gaza conflict, and the effect on ceasefire talks is not spelled out in these headlines.
items.analysis: Targeted strikes on senior commanders are a recurring feature of the conflict and can complicate any moves toward a broader truce.

items.headline: Netanyahu calls for a unity government as Eisenkot pushes back
items.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu says only a unity government can guarantee Israel's security, while opposition leader Eisenkot dismisses the call as a ploy.
items.detail: Netanyahu urged talks without preconditions on forming a unity government. Eisenkot rejected the prime minister's framing as spin, and reports say talks are already scheduled. Israel's new parliament has been sworn in, and Eisenkot is trying to build a government. Netanyahu's position is that a broad coalition is needed for security reasons, while the opposition sees it as a tactical move.
items.analysis: Whether a broad coalition forms will shape Israel's wartime decisions and its approach to Gaza and the wider region in the months ahead.

items.headline: Southeast Asian leaders meet in Manila as trade disruption takes centre stage
items.summary: The 49th ASEAN summit has opened in the Philippines, with a Trump visit adding focus to trade disruption across the region.
items.detail: ASEAN, the group of ten Southeast Asian nations, is holding its annual summit in Manila. Coverage highlights that global powers are converging on the city and that the US visit has put trade tensions at the top of the agenda. Member states differ on how closely to align with either Washington or Beijing, which is a recurring theme at these meetings.
items.analysis: The summit will show how Southeast Asian governments are balancing trade ties with the US and China as tariffs and supply chain shifts continue.

items.headline: US envoy Kushner aims to broker Europe-Russia talks on Ukraine
items.summary: US envoy Jared Kushner says he wants to broker talks between Europe and Russia on Ukraine, but the Kremlin says European negotiators have not yet reached out.
items.detail: Kushner has said he aims to bring Europe and Russia together on the Ukraine question. Russia's Kremlin said Europe's negotiators have not yet contacted it, which suggests a gap in how the talks would begin. Europe has recently chosen five countries to represent it in the peace discussions, according to earlier reports.
items.analysis: Whether Europe and Russia open a direct channel will determine how quickly any Ukraine peace process can move beyond the US-led track.

items.headline: Rahul Gandhi's 'no longer a democracy' remark sparks a fresh BJP-Congress clash
items.summary: Rahul Gandhi said at the Bharat Summit that India is no longer a democracy, and the BJP responded by calling him a puppet of foreign powers.
items.detail: Speaking at the Congress-organised Bharat Summit in Hyderabad, Gandhi said democracy had been weakened under BJP rule and questioned the legitimacy of the 2024 election results. The BJP's national media convenor Ashish Usha Agarwal accused him of seeking regime change with foreign help and of moving from opposition politics towards an anti-national stance. Reports also describe a row over a foreign politician's slogan at the event and questions about the summit's guests and foreign links.
items.analysis: The exchange reflects a deepening divide over the health of Indian democracy, with each side framing the other's statements as either legitimate criticism or a threat to the system.

items.headline: Election Commission assures Supreme Court that voters can re-apply without prosecution
items.summary: The Election Commission has told the Supreme Court that voters whose names were deleted in the roll revision can re-apply through Form 6 without fear of prosecution.
items.detail: The assurance relates to the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls, after which some names were removed. Voters who were deleted can apply again using Form 6, according to the Commission's submission. The reassurance was given in response to concerns raised before the court. Opposition parties have questioned the revision process more broadly, and the headlines do not include their latest response.
items.analysis: The assurance may ease fears among voters who were removed, but the wider debate over how rolls are revised is likely to continue as electoral calendars approach.

items.headline: Supreme Court says parents' salary alone cannot decide OBC creamy layer status
items.summary: The Supreme Court has said that a parent's salary alone cannot decide whether someone is excluded from OBC reservation benefits under the creamy layer rule.
items.detail: The creamy layer rule removes better-off families from reservation benefits for Other Backward Classes, and the test has long been contested. The court's remark indicates that income is one factor among others, rather than the sole basis for classification. The judgment will affect how state and central authorities apply the rule to individual applicants.
items.analysis: Changes in how creamy layer status is assessed can affect large numbers of OBC families and are closely followed by both beneficiaries and critics of reservation policy.

items.headline: Delhi court rejects bail for two accused in 2023 Parliament security breach
items.summary: A Delhi court has rejected bail pleas from two accused in the 2023 Parliament security breach case.
items.detail: The court described the episode in strong terms, reportedly calling it a planned, terror-like situation inside Parliament, and refused bail to the two men. The case concerns the breach of security in the Lok Sabha chamber in December 2023. The accused's lawyers and the prosecution's full arguments are not detailed in these headlines, and the trial continues.
items.analysis: The ruling keeps a high-profile security case in the courts and reflects the seriousness with which authorities are treating the breach.

items.headline: Kerala High Court floats lowering the juvenile age from 18 to 16
items.summary: The Kerala High Court has suggested that the age that defines a juvenile could be lowered from 18 to 16.
items.detail: The court raised the idea as part of a broader discussion about how the justice system treats young offenders. Under India's juvenile justice law, anyone below 18 is treated as a child, and a change would affect how serious cases involving older teenagers are handled. The suggestion is a proposal for debate rather than a ruling, and no government decision is reported in the headlines.
items.analysis: Any change to the juvenile age would be a major national policy question, so the court's remarks are likely to fuel debate among lawyers, child-rights groups and lawmakers.

items.headline: E Sreedharan proposes a 9-km sky metro for Kochi
items.summary: Metro planner E Sreedharan has proposed a 9-kilometre sky metro line for Kochi.
items.detail: Sreedharan, who is widely known as the architect of Delhi Metro, has put forward the plan for an elevated 9-km line in the city. The headlines do not give the route, cost or approval status. Kochi already runs a metro system, and additional lines are usually debated over funding, land and ridership.
items.analysis: Kochi's transport planning continues to be discussed as the city grows, and the feasibility of new lines depends on funding and approvals that are not yet detailed.

items.headline: CPI leader alleges Kerala government is surrendering education to RSS
items.summary: CPI leader Rajan has accused the Kerala government of surrendering education to the RSS and Sangh Parivar.
items.detail: The allegation was made publicly by a senior CPI figure, reflecting a political sensitivity around who influences the education system. The headlines do not include a detailed response from the government or the state's ruling front. Political debates over curriculum and institutions have been a recurring feature in Kerala politics.
items.analysis: Education policy is a politically charged area in Kerala, and the government's reply will matter for the debate between allied parties and the opposition.

items.headline: Cyclone warning for the Bay of Bengal affects Andaman ferries
items.summary: The IMD expects a severe cyclonic storm over the Bay of Bengal by November 17, with heavy rain alerts for the Andaman islands and possible ferry cancellations.
items.detail: Forecasts say a depression in the Bay of Bengal could strengthen into a severe cyclonic storm, which is being referred to as Cyclone Akvan. Andaman ferries may be cancelled as the system approaches, and heavy rain is expected over the islands. Tamil Nadu is expected to see less impact, according to earlier reports. Residents of the islands rely on ferries for supplies and travel, so cancellations can disrupt daily life.
items.analysis: Ferry cancellations are a practical concern for island communities, and the storm's track will decide how much disruption follows.

items.headline: LG flags climate risks facing the Andaman Islands
items.summary: The Lieutenant Governor of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands has highlighted the climate risks the islands face.
items.detail: The remarks put the islands' vulnerability to rising seas, storms and heavy rain in focus. The headlines do not spell out specific new measures. The islands have a fragile coastal and forest ecology, and the administration has been reviewing long-term planning, including a roadmap reviewed recently by NITI Aayog.
items.analysis: Climate exposure is central to planning for the islands, and how risks are weighed against development projects is likely to remain a live question.

items.headline: Climate leaders criticise Australia for weaker Just Transition ambition at COP31
items.summary: Climate leaders have criticised Australia for weakening its ambition on a Just Transition, the plan to protect workers and communities during the shift away from fossil fuels.
items.detail: The criticism came during the COP31 climate talks. Just Transition refers to making sure workers and regions dependent on coal and other fossil fuels are supported as economies change. Critics say weaker commitments in this area can make it harder to win support for deeper emissions cuts. The headlines do not include Australia's full reply.
items.analysis: How rich countries pair climate targets with support for affected workers is a key test of the COP process, and the debate will shape negotiations.

items.headline: UN warns climate change could force millions to move
items.summary: A UN warning says climate change could force millions of people to move from their homes.
items.detail: The warning points to rising displacement risks from floods, droughts and other climate impacts, particularly in vulnerable regions. Such movements can put pressure on cities and neighbouring areas and affect food and water supplies. The headlines do not include specific projections or new policy commitments.
items.analysis: Climate displacement is increasingly part of the global conversation on migration and adaptation, and it links environmental risk to economic and social planning.

items.headline: Universal Sompo names Amit Bhandari as managing director and CEO
items.summary: Universal Sompo General Insurance has appointed Amit Bhandari as managing director and CEO, subject to approval from the IRDAI.
items.detail: The appointment is subject to regulatory approval by the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India, as required for senior insurance leadership. Leadership changes at general insurers draw attention because they can signal shifts in strategy, distribution and growth priorities. The headlines do not give details on Bhandari's background or the company's plans.
items.analysis: Insurers' top leadership changes are often watched by investors and brokers, and approval from the regulator is the next step to confirm the move.

items.headline: Star Health expects 19% growth in gross written premium to Rs 24,000 crore in FY27
items.summary: Star Health's managing director expects gross written premium to grow 19 percent to Rs 24,000 crore in FY27.
items.detail: Gross written premium is the total premium an insurer has written before reinsurance, a common measure of business volume. Star Health is one of India's largest standalone health insurers, and its growth outlook is closely watched by investors and policyholders. The projection depends on premium growth, claims trends and regulatory changes that the headlines do not detail.
items.analysis: Health insurance growth in India is tied to rising medical costs and awareness, and forecasts like this set expectations for the sector's next financial year.

items.headline: Pollution-linked health insurance claims rise 4.3 times in three years
items.summary: A report says pollution-linked health insurance claims have risen 4.3 times over three years.
items.detail: The report links a sharp increase in claims to air pollution, a concern in many Indian cities during winter months. Rising claims affect insurers' pricing and risk models, and can prompt questions about how pollution-related illnesses are covered. The headlines do not give the full breakdown of the data or the sources used.
items.analysis: If pollution-related claims keep rising, insurers may need to adjust pricing and underwriting, and policyholders may see changes in premiums or cover.

items.headline: UAE flight schedules revised as cancellations and delays continue
items.summary: Airlines serving the UAE have revised schedules, with fresh cancellations and delays reported, and a Gulf airspace warning runs until November 16.
items.detail: Gulf News reports that airlines are changing timetables as regional tensions continue, and passengers are advised to check with carriers before travel. Dubai flights to and from Israeli carriers remain suspended amid a security dispute that keeps those airlines out of the UAE. A Gulf airspace warning is due to expire on November 16, which affects routes ahead of upcoming international events.
items.analysis: Travellers through Dubai and other Gulf hubs should expect shifting schedules until airspace warnings are lifted and airlines settle their plans.

items.headline: Air India suspends Riyadh, Dammam and Jeddah flights
items.summary: Air India and Air India Express have suspended flights to Riyadh and Dammam until November 30, and to Jeddah until November 21.
items.detail: The suspensions cover major Saudi cities that are important for the Indian diaspora and pilgrimage travel. The airlines have not been quoted in these headlines on the full reasons, but the suspensions come amid heightened regional security concerns. Passengers booked on these routes will need to rebook or seek refunds according to airline policy.
items.analysis: The longer suspensions indicate airlines are planning for prolonged disruption rather than a short pause, which affects travel between India and the Saudi Gulf.

items.headline: Saudi-led coalition intercepts Houthi missiles and drones as Bahrain issues alert
items.summary: The Saudi-led coalition says it intercepted missiles heading toward Riyadh and drones over the Eastern Province, while Bahrain issued a threat alert.
items.detail: Reports describe the coalition intercepting ballistic missiles and drones, with Houthi involvement cited in several outlets. Bahrain warned of potential threats as the interceptions were reported. The Gulf region remains on heightened alert, and residents have been advised to follow official updates. The headlines do not describe any casualties or damage.
items.analysis: Repeated interceptions across several Gulf states show the regional security situation is still active, which matters for airlines, insurers and residents.

items.headline: Nifty closes at 25,144 after its third straight weekly gain
items.summary: The Nifty closed at 25,144 after a third straight weekly gain, with smallcaps up 3.6 percent and PSU banks surging 7.5 percent.
items.detail: The gains came in a week when foreign investors returned to Indian equities and the market recovered from a six-month low set in October, according to earlier reports. Analysts cited support in the 24,800 to 25,000 range for the index. The rally has been driven partly by a rotation out of AI-heavy stocks and into Indian markets, though the headlines describe the move as still fragile.
items.analysis: The strength of the rally depends on whether foreign flows continue and whether crude prices and inflation stay under control.

items.headline: FPIs pour Rs 84,290 crore into equities in the first fortnight of November
items.summary: Foreign portfolio investors put Rs 84,290 crore into Indian equities in the first two weeks of November.
items.detail: The inflow marks a sharp turnaround after earlier outflows, and reports describe it as a signal of renewed foreign confidence in India. Analysts attribute the change to shifting global flows and the relative appeal of Indian stocks after a correction. Such flows can move the rupee and the broader index, and they are sensitive to US interest rate expectations.
items.analysis: Sustained foreign buying would support the market, but flows can reverse quickly when global rates or oil prices shift.

items.headline: Rupee weakens 33 paise as crude and a firm dollar weigh
items.summary: The rupee has weakened by 33 paise against the dollar, closing near 94.20 as crude prices and a strong dollar put pressure on it.
items.detail: A stronger dollar and higher oil prices increase India's import bill, which tends to weigh on the rupee. Rising crude also feeds into inflation concerns, which the markets have been watching closely. Reports point to expectations of US rate moves as an additional source of dollar strength. The rupee's level and direction will be watched by importers, exporters and anyone sending money abroad.
items.analysis: A weaker rupee makes imports costlier, while helping exporters and remittance recipients, so the currency is a balancing act for the economy.

items.headline: Bitcoin falls below $64,000 as ETF outflows run for a seventh day
items.summary: Bitcoin has fallen below $64,000 as outflows from exchange-traded funds extended to a seventh straight day.
items.detail: The decline reflects a broader pullback in crypto risk appetite, with reports describing leveraged positions being liquidated. Analysts link part of the weakness to rate expectations in the US, which have made investors more cautious about speculative assets. The headlines describe the move as a four-month low for the token.
items.analysis: Crypto prices are often seen as a gauge of risk appetite, and continued ETF outflows suggest investors are reducing exposure.

items.headline: Google's Android XR glasses will block facial recognition and hide faces from Gemini
items.summary: Google's Android XR smart glasses will hide faces from its Gemini assistant and ban real-time facial recognition, with Samsung announcing pricing and sale details.
items.detail: The privacy design choice means the glasses are built to avoid identifying people in real time, a feature that has drawn concern from privacy advocates about wearable cameras. Samsung has announced pricing and sale details, developed with Google. The headlines do not specify markets or dates for launch beyond the announcement.
items.analysis: Building privacy limits into camera-equipped wearables is becoming a competitive and regulatory issue, and how these rules work in practice will matter for adoption.

items.headline: Samsung moves from AI chips toward building its own data centres
items.summary: Samsung, which has gained ground in AI chips, now wants to build data centres.
items.detail: The Financial Times reports that the company's success in AI memory and chips has led it to move into the data centre business. Data centres are where AI models are trained and run, so a chipmaker entering the space could change its relationship with cloud and AI customers. The headlines do not give investment figures or partners.
items.analysis: The move would make Samsung a bigger player across the AI supply chain, from memory chips to the facilities that run them.

items.headline: South Korea's October ICT exports hit $70.35 billion on AI memory boom
items.summary: South Korea's ICT exports reached $70.35 billion in October, driven by a boom in AI memory chips.
items.detail: The figure reflects strong demand for memory chips used in AI servers, which has lifted South Korean exports sharply. One report describes the monthly growth rate as above 200 percent, a sign of how quickly demand has shifted. The headlines frame this as an AI-led supercycle in memory products.
items.analysis: South Korea's export numbers are a useful signal of global AI hardware demand, and they also show how concentrated the boom is in a few chip categories.

items.headline: Nature collection looks at turning plastics and biomass into useful chemicals with solid catalysts
items.summary: A Nature collection is gathering research on converting plastics and biomass-derived polymers using heterogeneous catalysis.
items.detail: Heterogeneous catalysis uses solid catalysts that help chemical reactions happen on their surfaces, which makes separating and reusing them easier than with dissolved catalysts. Converting plastic waste and plant-based polymers into fuels or chemicals is a major goal for recycling and a lower-carbon chemical industry. The collection brings together studies on how such catalysts can be designed and tested.
items.analysis: Solid catalysts that can break down polymers efficiently are a key target for circular-economy chemistry, though scaling from the lab remains difficult.

items.headline: Defective UiO-66 catalyst converts methane to acetic acid
items.summary: Researchers report that a defect-engineered version of the UiO-66 material can convert methane into acetic acid.
items.detail: UiO-66 is a metal-organic framework, a porous crystalline material with a large internal surface area that can host chemical reactions. Methane, the main component of natural gas, is abundant but hard to convert into more useful liquid chemicals. Introducing defects into the framework can change how it binds and activates molecules, which is the approach the study uses.
items.analysis: Turning methane into liquid products at modest conditions would be valuable for chemicals and fuels, but the findings need to be tested at larger scales.

items.headline: Curated hydrogen database links storage capacity to release pressure
items.summary: A curated database of hydrogen storage materials has revealed links between how much hydrogen a material can hold and the pressure at which it releases it.
items.detail: Storing hydrogen safely and densely is a central problem for hydrogen fuel, whether in vehicles, ships or aviation. By collecting data from many studies in one place, the database lets researchers look for trade-offs between capacity and release conditions. Such databases can also help computational screening of promising candidates before lab work begins.
items.analysis: Better data on storage trade-offs can speed up the search for materials that make hydrogen practical in transport, a field where progress has been slow.

items.headline: AI identifies overlooked two-dimensional MXenes in materials databases
items.summary: An AI-based approach has picked out previously overlooked two-dimensional MXene materials in existing materials science databases.
items.detail: MXenes are a family of ultrathin two-dimensional materials built from metal carbides, nitrides or carbonitrides, and they are studied for batteries, electronics and catalysis. Many possible MXene compositions have been proposed but not fully explored. Using machine learning to scan existing databases can find candidates that were missed by traditional searching, which can then be tested by experiment or detailed calculation.
items.analysis: Data-driven screening of known databases is a cheap way to find new materials, though predicted candidates still need experimental confirmation.

items.headline: Earth's oldest animals were preserved by ancient underwater canyons
items.summary: A study suggests that ancient underwater canyons helped preserve some of Earth's oldest animal fossils.
items.detail: The research points to the way sediment flowing through submarine canyons can rapidly bury soft-bodied organisms, protecting them from decay. Fossils of early animals are rare because such bodies usually do not survive, so the mechanism helps explain gaps in the record. The finding has received far less public attention than many other science stories this week.
items.analysis: Understanding how early animals were preserved can shape where scientists look for the first complex life and how they read the fossil record.

items.headline: A dead star flashes radio waves every 8 minutes, and its partner looks like the sun
items.summary: Astronomers have traced a long-period radio transient that flashes every few minutes to a binary system with a dead star and a Sun-like companion.
items.detail: Since 2022, astronomers have been puzzling over a new class of cosmic objects that emit bright radio flashes at intervals of minutes to hours. Some have now been linked to binary systems in which a small, cool dead star pairs with a companion. The explanation is still being tested, and the object has received limited coverage beyond specialist outlets.
items.analysis: Each new case helps astronomers narrow down which kinds of binary systems can produce these puzzling radio signals.
